extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, assignees/owners, applicants, and USPTO staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on who may act in U.S. patent matters and the documentary, signature, timing, and recordation requirements for establishing an assignee's right to request or take action before the USPTO (pre- and post-September 16, 2012 rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may take action in patent matters (pre- and post- Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: A national patent application is owned by (A) the inventor(s); (B) an assignee or multiple assignees of the inventor(s); or (C) some combination of the assignee(s) and inventors who have not assigned away their right, title and interest. A single assignee of the entire right, title and interest may act alone; otherwise all partial assignees and inventors who together own the entire right, title and interest must act together to conduct prosecution. (See pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.71(b)(1)-(2) and 37 CFR 3.71(b) / 37 CFR 3.73(a)-(c).)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a single assignee of the entire right, that assignee may act alone (subject to making the assignee of record). If there are partial assignees or a mixture of assignees and inventors, the combination of all owners is needed to conduct prosecution unless specific regulatory relief (e.g., petition under 1.47 / 1.46(b)(2)) has been granted. Post-September 16, 2012 rules parallel pre-AIA rules (37 CFR 3.71/3.73) but require additional procedural compliance (becoming applicant under 1.46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership (pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee who first seeks to take action in a matter (filed before Sept. 16, 2012) must establish ownership to the satisfaction of the Director by submitting to the Office, in the Office file related to the matter: (A) documentary evidence of a chain of title from the original owner to the assignee (e.g., copy of an executed assignment submitted for recording) and a statement affirming the documentary evidence was or is being submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11; or (B) a statement specifying, by reel and frame number, where such evidence is recorded in the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents submitted to establish ownership are required to be recorded or submitted for recordation under 37 CFR 3.11 as a condition to permitting the assignee to take action. The establishment of ownership can be combined with the paper requesting or taking action. Failure to include the submission establishing ownership prior to or at the same time as the action will result in the action not being given effect; a later submission will make that later date the date of the request or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership for applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 (37 CFR 3.73(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee who is not the original applicant must establish ownership to the satisfaction of the Director by submitting a signed statement identifying the assignee accompanied by either documentary evidence of chain of title plus a statement affirming recordation under 37 CFR 3.11, or by a statement specifying where documentary evidence is recorded (reel/frame). The assignee must also become the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 (request to change applicant) and file an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 37 CFR 3.73(c) statement must be filed in the Office file related to the matter and signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee or by a patent practitioner of record. Documents must be recorded per 37 CFR 3.11. Once 37 CFR 3.73(c) is complied with, the assignee may continue to take action without refiling the statement unless ownership changes. The ownership-establishing statement and request to change applicant must be submitted prior to or at the same time as the paper requesting or taking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of ownership establishment submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The establishment of ownership by the assignee must be submitted prior to, or at the same time as, the paper requesting or taking action. If the submission establishing ownership is not present, the action sought to be taken will not be given effect. If the submission establishing ownership is submitted at a later date, that later date will be the date of the request for action or the date of the assignee’s action taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ownership-establishing submission and any required request to change applicant (post-2012) can be combined with the action paper. Timeliness is dispositive: untimely proof means the Office treats the action as not effective until the date the ownership is established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required when multiple partial assignees exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than one assignee holds rights, each partial assignee must provide a submission under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) / 37 CFR 3.73(c) and in each submission the extent of each assignee’s interest must be set forth so the Office can determine whether the entire right, title and interest has been obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the extent of a partial assignee’s ownership interest is not set forth, the Office may refuse to accept the submission as establishing ownership. Acceptable approaches include (i) specifying (by percentage) the extent of ownership to account for the entire right, or (ii) identifying the parties (including inventors) who together own the entire interest and stating that all identified parties own the entire right, title and interest (37 CFR 3.73(c)(2)(i)-(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting ownership statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are two or more conflicting 37 CFR 3.73(b)/(c) statements in an application or other Office proceeding, the statement with the latest date of submission will normally control as to establishment of the assignee. If ownership established as controlling is contested on the record by another party who submitted a conflicting statement, the matter shall be forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (or the Director will determine who may control prosecution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, where conflicting statements exist the ownership entity that filed the application will be permitted to conduct prosecution and other parties with conflicting statements may consider filing their own application. Post-2012 rules explicitly state the Director will determine which purported assignee may control prosecution (37 CFR 3.73(c)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign the ownership submission (authorized signatories)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission establishing ownership must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. For organizations, the submission may be signed: (A) by a person in the organization having apparent authority to sign (officers such as CEO, president, vice-president, secretary, treasurer are presumed to have authority; chairman acceptable; individual director not acceptable); (B) by any person if the submission states that the person is authorized to act on behalf of the assignee; (C) by a person empowered by an organizational resolution if a copy of the resolution is or was previously submitted in the record; or (D) for patent matters post-2012, by a practitioner of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles in foreign countries (Manager, Director) are normally presumed to be officers. Persons with titles that do not clearly indicate officer status (administrator, general counsel) are not presumed to have authority unless the submission clearly indicates their authority. A power of attorney to a patent practitioner to prosecute does not make that practitioner an official of the assignee or empower the practitioner to sign the submission on behalf of the assignee (unless the practitioner is of record and meets the criteria in 37 CFR 3.73(d)(3)). Where a submission does not comply with (A)-(D), evidence of authority will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When ownership must be established (examples of actions requiring ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership must be established under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) / 37 CFR 3.73(c) when the assignee: signs a request for status of an application or gives a power to inspect an application; appoints its own registered attorney or agent to prosecute an application; signs a disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321; consents to the filing of a reissue application; consents to the correction of inventorship in a patent; or signs a Fee(s) Transmittal (PTOL-85B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective Sept. 16, 2012, a juristic entity (organization) that is an owner/assignee must be represented by a patent practitioner for many papers. See MPEP cross-references for each type of action. The list in the MPEP is illustrative and not necessarily exhaustive; when in doubt, establish ownership before acting.

rubrics_metrics.name: When ownership need not be established (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership need not be established under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) / 37 CFR 3.73(c) for certain papers, such as signing a small entity statement (37 CFR 1.27), signing a statement of common ownership of two inventions, signing a NASA or DOE property rights statement, signing an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131(a) where the inventor is unavailable, signing a certificate under 37 CFR 1.8, or filing a request for reexamination of a patent under 37 CFR 1.510.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific exceptions indicate situations where an assignee's formal establishment of ownership is not required to sign certain administrative statements. Consult the cited MPEP sections for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording requirement for documents establishing ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted to establish ownership are required to be recorded, or submitted for recordation pursuant to 37 CFR 3.11, as a condition to permitting the assignee to take action in a matter pending before the Office. 35 U.S.C. 261 requires transfer of ownership by an assignment to be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission of documentary evidence must be accompanied by a statement affirming the documentary evidence was or is being submitted for recordation under 37 CFR 3.11, or must specify where the documentary evidence is recorded (reel/frame). Failure to record may prevent the Office from recognizing the assignee's right to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing applications and CPA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When an assignee files a continuation or divisional application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) (filed before Sept. 16, 2012) the application papers must contain either (A) a copy of a statement filed under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) in the parent application, or (B) a newly executed statement under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b). For continuation-in-part applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012 by an assignee, a newly executed statement under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) must be filed. For CPAs in design applications, the statement in the parent will serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For continuing applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, analogous requirements apply under 37 CFR 3.73(c). The parent application's ownership statement may carry forward in many continuing prosecution contexts (including RCEs), but where required the assignee must supply a new statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Continued Examination (RCE) continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) is filed under 37 CFR 1.114, the application is not considered abandoned and the statement under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) or under 37 CFR 3.73(c) in the application will continue to serve as the statement establishing ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE does not ordinarily require a new ownership submission if a valid 3.73 statement is already of record; ensure the existing statement meets the applicable requirements for recordation and authorized signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee must become applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 when not original applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee who is not the original applicant must become the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46 in order to request or take action in a patent application. A request to change the applicant under 37 CFR 1.46(c)(2) must be filed and must be accompanied by an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 specifying the applicant in the applicant information section and comply with 37 CFR 3.71 and 37 CFR 3.73.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Becoming the applicant requires both the procedural change of applicant and the ownership-establishing statement; both must be present prior to or at the same time as the action to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of power of attorney on authority to sign ownership statements
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney (37 CFR 1.32(b)(4)) to a patent practitioner to prosecute a patent application executed by the applicant or the assignee of the entire interest does not by itself make that practitioner an official of an assignee or empower the practitioner to sign the submission on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent practitioner may sign a 37 CFR 3.73(c) statement if the practitioner is of record (appointed in a power of attorney already of record, or if the 3.73(c) statement is accompanied by a power of attorney appointing the practitioner who signed). Otherwise, the submission must show the signatory's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms that may be used to establish ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/96 may be used to establish ownership under pre-AIA 37 CFR 3.73(b) (and analogous forms/approaches for post-2012 statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A duplicate copy of a 37 CFR 3.73(b) or 3.73(c) statement is not required and should not be submitted. See 37 CFR 1.4(b) and MPEP § 502.04 for duplication guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juristic entity signature and representation rules (post-Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective September 16, 2012, an owner or assignee that is a juristic entity must be represented by a patent practitioner. Juristic entities may sign small entity assertions (37 CFR 1.27), disclaimers (37 CFR 1.321), submissions under 37 CFR 3.73 to establish ownership, powers of attorney under 37 CFR 1.32 and powers to inspect under 37 CFR 1.14. However, any other paper submitted on behalf of a juristic entity on or after September 16, 2012, must be signed by a patent practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the specific paper type: some administrative papers remain signable by juristic entities, but most other filings must bear a practitioner signature for the Office to accept them when submitted on behalf of an organization.
